case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
title: Meet the Real F-35A
tests: Tests whether a short factual aircraft film preserves the named variant's visible geometry and operating characteristics.

faults.what: The aircraft is not a recognizable F-35A: the airborne views clearly show two separated rear exhausts rather than one, with an incorrect fuselage and cockpit configuration.
All three requested on-screen labels are absent from the supplied frames.
Aircraft details appear to morph during takeoff, particularly the cockpit profile and rear engine geometry.
The narration awkwardly introduces the aircraft as 'The person F-35A.'

judge.summary: The widescreen clip depicts a runway takeoff and flight, but shows the wrong aircraft configuration and omits every requested label.

must_haves.item: The aircraft has the recognizable F-35 configuration: one rear engine exhaust, two outward-canted vertical tails and no canards.
must_haves.why: Two separated rear exhausts are clearly visible in the airborne views, contradicting the F-35A's single-engine configuration.

must_haves.item: The takeoff shows a forward runway roll and lift-off, not hovering or a vertical launch.
must_haves.why: The sequence progresses from wheels on the runway to forward flight above it, with increasing ground clearance.

must_haves.item: The same aircraft design remains consistent between the runway and airborne views.
must_haves.why: The cockpit profile and rear engine geometry visibly change rather than maintaining a stable, coherent aircraft model.

must_haves.item: All three requested labels appear exactly and are legible.
must_haves.why: None of the requested labels is visible in the supplied frames.

must_haves.item: Audible English narration correctly describes one engine and conventional runway takeoff without attributing F-35B hover capability to the F-35A.
must_haves.why: Despite the awkward introductory wording, the supplied transcript states that the F-35A has one engine and takes off from a conventional runway, without mentioning hover capability.

title: Seed Growth With Supplied Narration
tests: Tests whether a supplied script becomes verbatim audible narration synchronized with an explanatory visual sequence.

exact_text.text: A seed takes in water. Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.
exact_text.read_as: A seed takes in water. Roots grow downward.

faults.what: The voice-over omits the entire clause about the shoot reaching up toward the light.
The starting object looks like a large, glossy red flower bud rather than a recognizable seed, then changes into a leafy plant with an unusually bulky, exposed root crown.

The required growth sequence is not clearly explained: water reaching the seed is not shown in the supplied frames, and large leaves are already present at 3 seconds before the downward roots become clearly visible at 5 seconds.
The detailed, photorealistic glass-tank scene does not match the requested simple animation.

judge.summary: The 8-second widescreen clip shows a plant developing in a glass tank, but the narration is incomplete and the seed-to-sprout sequence is unclear.

must_haves.item: One approximately 8-second widescreen video shows an animated seed sprouting.
must_haves.why: The duration and widescreen format are correct, and the plant changes across frames, but the starting object resembles a red flower bud rather than a recognizable seed sprouting.

must_haves.item: The audible voice-over says the supplied script verbatim, without extra spoken lines.
must_haves.why: The supplied audio transcript ends at 'Roots grow downward.' and omits the remaining script.

must_haves.item: Water reaches the seed, roots grow downward, and a shoot grows upward toward light in that order.
must_haves.why: Water reaching the seed is not demonstrated in the frames, and leafy upward growth is visible before clear downward roots. A later shoot does extend toward the overhead light.

must_haves.item: The corresponding growth stages appear while the narration describes them.
must_haves.why: Water uptake is not clearly depicted, and the upward shoot stage has no corresponding narration because that clause is missing.

must_haves.item: There is no on-screen text or music.
must_haves.why: No on-screen text is visible, but the supplied sound information does not establish whether music is absent.

case_name: A film brief the agent already made on the free tier: the economists' video podcast
title: Two economists, a 30 s video podcast
tests: Tests whether a system can turn a story brief with two named characters and four spoken lines into a 30-second film: characters that persist across shots, audible dialogue that carries the argument, and a staged studio.

faults.what: The supplied audio transcript contains only one Keynesian line; Maya's second line and both of Leo's lines are missing, leaving the requested economic debate incomplete.
The ending shows friendly smiles and raised mugs, but there is no audible disagreement or closing exchange.
The lettering on the mugs appears garbled and changes across the sampled frames.

judge.summary: The clip delivers an attractive, consistent live-action podcast setting, but only one audible line instead of the requested four-line debate.

must_haves.item: Two hosts, a woman and a man, are on screen at microphones in a cosy studio with a live-action look, not animation.
must_haves.why: All four frames show a woman and a man seated at microphones in a warmly furnished studio with a realistic live-action appearance.

must_haves.item: Each host is heard speaking two short lines: Maya argues the government should spend in a recession to restore demand; Leo argues spending and cheap money cause boom and bust and the economy should correct itself.
must_haves.why: The only transcribed speech is one line advocating government spending to restore demand; neither two lines per host nor Leo's argument is present.

must_haves.item: The lines are audible speech, not only music or silence.
must_haves.why: The sound report confirms audible speech, although it contains only one of the requested lines.

must_haves.item: The two hosts stay the same people across the shots.
must_haves.why: The hosts' faces, hair, and clothing remain consistent across the supplied frames.

must_haves.item: It ends on a friendly disagreement between them.
must_haves.why: The final sampled frame is friendly, but the supplied speech contains no opposing position or closing disagreement.

must_haves.item: About 30 seconds, widescreen 16:9.
must_haves.why: The reported duration is 30 seconds, and the supplied frames are 16:9.

case_name: A 10-second product ad with a closing line (the live bench's film brief)
title: Cabin Coffee, 10 s YouTube ad
tests: Tests a short ad from a one-line brief: a staged product moment, a human action, and an exact closing line on screen.

faults.what: No hand lifts the mug in the supplied frames; it remains on the table throughout.
The required closing words 'Wake up slow' are absent from the supplied ending frame.
No visible Cabin Coffee branding identifies the advertiser.
The audio transcript reports unrelated speech, 'Yhteiskunnalliset.', which does not fit the requested ad.

judge.summary: The clip delivers a warm, steaming-mug scene but omits the hand lift, closing slogan, and visible Cabin Coffee identity.

must_haves.item: A steaming mug on a wooden table in dawn light is the opening image.
must_haves.why: The first supplied frame shows a steaming mug on a wooden table in warm, low morning-style window light.

must_haves.item: A hand lifts the mug.
must_haves.why: No hand appears in any supplied frame, and the mug remains on the table.

must_haves.item: The words 'Wake up slow' appear on screen at the end, spelled exactly.
must_haves.why: No text appears in the supplied ending frame.

must_haves.item: The mood is warm and quiet (no fast cuts, no loud colours).
must_haves.why: The frames maintain a consistent, softly lit composition with warm muted colours; the reported audio peak is very low.

must_haves.item: About 10 seconds, widescreen 16:9.
must_haves.why: The clip is reported as 10 seconds, and the supplied frames are 16:9.

case_name: A one-minute explainer with a fixed sequence of facts: the citric acid cycle
title: Citric acid cycle, a 60 s explainer
tests: Tests a one-minute explainer with a fixed order of facts: whether the system keeps one consistent diagram across a minute, letters short labels correctly, narrates the steps in order, and stays within the length.

faults.what: The title is misspelled as 'Citric acid vycle', and the diagram contains extensive garbled, scientifically unusable labels.
The frames show several disconnected faint circles rather than a readable Krebs-cycle pathway connecting the required reactions and products.
The required acetyl-CoA entry, citrate formation, two CO2 releases, energy-carrier production, and oxaloacetate regeneration are not visibly communicated.
The supplied speech only states where the cycle occurs; it does not explain the requested steps as they happen.
The mitochondrion-like diagram changes shape and enlarges across the sampled frames without a clear instructional purpose.

judge.summary: The 60-second widescreen clip shows a mitochondrion-like cartoon, but garbled labels, an incorrect title, and missing reaction explanations make it unusable as a biology explainer.

must_haves.item: The cycle is shown as a loop, as a simple clean 2D animation inside a mitochondrion, not live action.
must_haves.why: The imagery is a 2D mitochondrion-like drawing, but no coherent cycle loop is shown; the internal circles are disconnected.

must_haves.item: The steps appear in order: acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to form citrate; two carbons leave as CO2; NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced; oxaloacetate is regenerated.
must_haves.why: None of this reaction sequence is identifiable in the supplied frames or narration.

must_haves.item: Calm English narration is audible and explains each step as it happens.
must_haves.why: English speech is reported, but its only supplied sentence describes the mitochondrial location rather than explaining each step.

must_haves.item: The key molecules are labelled on screen as they appear, and the title 'Citric acid cycle' is shown.
must_haves.why: The title reads 'Citric acid vycle', and the molecule labels are missing or garbled.

must_haves.item: About 60 seconds, widescreen 16:9.
must_haves.why: The clip is reported as 60 seconds, and the supplied frames are 16:9.

must_haves.item: No music.
must_haves.why: The speech transcript and peak level do not establish whether background music is absent.
